findings.text: code_provenance() (pin.py:42-74) duplicates the capability the repository already owns at scripts/west_iron_galerkin_pair/measure.py:277 and at scripts/iron_graded_refinement/measure.py:77: the same git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no refusal, rev-parse HEAD, hash-object and rev-parse <rev>:<path> comparison, with only the error wording changed. pin.py already imports DISTANCES, SOURCE, SOURCE_SHA256, machine_source, save and source_field from the first owner, so the helper is copied from a module it is already coupled to rather than extended or wrapped. reckon/clones.py runs a textual clone detector at promotion, so this may also be raised mechanically. It matters because three near-identical provenance implementations now diverge independently whenever the stamping contract changes.

The pin is written at /work/projects/imas_gpu/nova/evidence/iron-core-magnetisation/west-62751/mesh-pair/inputs/west-62751-solve-inputs.json while the tracked constant REFERENCE at scripts/west_iron_galerkin_pair/measure.py:40-43 still resolves under /work/projects/imas_gpu/sophelio. The verifier makes west_inputs() pass only by assigning graded.REFERENCE in-process (verify.py:181), so west_inputs() still raises FileNotFoundError on the production path and the three nodes the brief names (the operator-bound WEST checks, the section 6 field-source re-measure and the 8/40 refinement) stay blocked until the shared-root section, section 7 of docs/plans/kernel-compile-barrier.html:84-86, repoints the tracked defaults. The manifest records this handoff in evidence_inputs, but the fragment states 'west_inputs() passes' without saying that the production reference still points elsewhere, which a reader can mistake for the dependency being unblocked.

The 'committed' values the nineteen comparisons check against are constants transcribed into the verifier (verify.py:28-36), not read from the fragments, the plan or tests/test_magnetisation.py that each row cites as its source. I checked the transcriptions against the committed records at 8d452b558 and they are correct (icm-west-62751-galerkin-pair.html:43 gives 7024.08/4396.82/1799.96 uT, icm-law-fit.html:21-22 gives 215.11019 and 1037.9637, tests/test_magnetisation.py:586 asserts mu[0] at 215.11019), so no number is wrong. The weakness is structural: a value mis-transcribed into both the verifier and the new fragment would compare equal and pass, so the fragment's claim that 'Each row compares the regenerated pin with the record that holds the number' overstates the independence the check achieves.
